steps.title: Slide the bottom panel into the open frame
steps.instruction: Keep the previously assembled panels (nodes 1, 3 and 21) fixed at their final source transforms. As shown in the large drawing of page 9 step 3, bring the bottom panel (node 2) horizontally into the open frame and slide it in the parent -X direction until it reaches its final source position with its side edges engaged along the two side panels. Follow the left inset: align the fitting and slot as shown, and avoid the crossed-out misaligned engagement. If the panel binds, withdraw it slightly, realign it, and slide it again; do not force it. Keep fingers clear of the closing edges and fittings.
warnings: Pinch/crush hazard: keep fingers clear of the panel edges and fittings while the bottom panel is slid into the frame.
The inset marks a misaligned fitting engagement as wrong; align the fitting in its slot before sliding the panel fully in.
Ensure the previously joined panels are fully seated before sliding the bottom panel; this animation does not verify their connection.
This motion is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure.
uncertainties: Mapping of the moving grey panel: it is mapped to node 2 ('bottom panel 35x25') because node 2 is a large horizontal panel that ends in contact with side panels 3 and 21 (large-component contact candidates [2,3] and [2,21], gap 0.0 m), while the other horizontal large panel, node 1, is already docked from the previous context.

Node 1 ('top panel 35x25') is retained as a fixed previously visible component per the tentative prior plan. Page 9 step 3 alone does not identify it by number; the illustrated frame orientation is schematic and may not match its horizontal source orientation in the finished cabinet.

Nodes 3 and 21 are mapped to the two fixed side panels of the illustrated open frame because both are large side panels and both are contact candidates with node 2. Because they are symmetric opposite side panels, the assignment of left/right is inferred, not proven by the drawing.

The 0.12 m start offset along parent +X is an inferred presentation gap only; the manual gives no travel distance. The direction is inferred from the illustrated insertion arrow, assuming the open front is +X and the panel moves toward -X into the frame; if the arrow represents the opposite approach, the motion direction would be wrong.

The illustration shows a fitting-and-slot alignment inset; the source nodes for the small connector hardware are not unambiguously identified by part number on page 9, so no separate hardware nodes are animated or listed as visible.

The drawing could be interpreted as inserting the back panel or another large panel rather than the bottom panel; node 4 ('back panel 35x25') is vertical in the source and was not chosen because the illustrated moving panel is horizontal. If that interpretation is correct, this node mapping and motion are invalid.
No torque, turn count, cam-lock rotation, or fastener tightening sequence is proposed because none is readable for this step.
Collision, groove clearance, and connector insertion are not modeled; the straight-line path may not represent the real insertion path.

validation: Structure, source hashes, node references, page bounds, and docking endpoints checked. Physical correctness and collision-free paths are not established.

steps.title: Slide top panel onto side panel edge and seat the connector fittings
steps.instruction: Keep the side panel (node 3) in its final position and bring the top panel (node 1) to it horizontally, moving along the parent-coordinate Z direction until the panel edge meets the side panel edge and the protruding connector hardware engages the keyhole slots, as shown in the large drawing and the lower-left detail (left-pointing arrow). Follow the upper-left inset: the fittings must be aligned in their slots as shown on the right; the crossed-out version shows an attempt made with the fittings misaligned and must be avoided. After the panels are pushed together, press the joint down at the corner as shown in the lower-right detail to seat the panels; this downward seating press ends at the panels’ final source positions and is therefore not animated in this step. Do not force the panels; if the fittings do not line up, separate, realign and slide again. Watch the hand positions shown in the detail and keep fingers clear of the closing gap.
warnings: Pinch/crush hazard: the illustration shows hands on the panel edges while the joint closes; keep fingers out of the closing gap and off the connector fittings.
The upper-left inset explicitly marks a misaligned fitting engagement as wrong (crossed out); engage the fittings in their slots before sliding the panels fully together.
This motion is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure.
uncertainties: Mapping of the two illustrated panels: the left panel of the drawing is mapped to side panel node 3 (plane at z ≈ -0.166 m, parent coordinates) and the right, moving panel to top panel node 1 (horizontal panel whose edge overlaps the side panel by geometry), because nodes 1 and 3 are listed as a large-component contact candidate with bounds gap 0.0 m.

The drawing does not identify parts by number, so the mirrored alternative side panel node 21 (the opposite side panel) would fit the same picture equally well; node 3 was chosen arbitrarily among the two symmetric side panels.

The illustrated panels could instead correspond to side panel plus bottom panel (node 2) rather than top panel (node 1); both are equally sized and both are contact candidates with the side panels. This was not resolved from page 8.

Start displacement of 0.05 m along +Z is an inferred presentation offset only; the manual gives no travel distance or start gap, and the direction (+Z, i.e. sliding the top panel in -Z toward the side panel edge) is inferred from the left-pointing arrow in the lower-left detail rather than from measured geometry.

The lower-right detail shows a downward press at the corner; that seating motion is not animated because a single track must end at the final zero offset, and no separate press distance is documented.

Connector hardware visible in the page (cam/dowel fittings such as the 139434, 139435 and 141413 positions in the inventory) is not shown as visible or animated, because the drawing gives no part numbers that can be unambiguously matched to those source nodes.

Panel orientation during assembly (panels drawn upright in the illustration while the source top panel is horizontal in the finished assembly) is not represented; only the join path in parent coordinates is proposed.
No torque, turn count or fastener tightening sequence is proposed, because none is readable on the selected page.

steps.title: Lower the opposite side panel onto the open edge of the two-panel corner
steps.instruction: Keep the already joined panels (nodes 1 and 3) fixed at their final source transforms. As shown by the downward arrow on page 9 step 2, bring the opposite side panel (node 21) straight down onto the open edge of the two-panel corner. Lower it until its mating edge reaches the final source position against the top panel connector edge. Do not force the joint; if the edge does not seat freely, lift the panel slightly, realign it, and lower it again. Keep hands clear of the closing edge.
warnings: Pinch/crush hazard: keep fingers clear of the closing edge while lowering the panel.
This motion is an unreviewed geometric proposal, not a verified assembly procedure.
Do not force the joint; if the fittings do not align, lift the panel, realign it, and lower it again.
The two fixed panels must already be fully seated before this step; this animation does not verify their connection.
uncertainties: Page 9 step 2 has no part numbers. The stationary two-panel body is inherited from the prior proposal as top panel node 1 and side panel node 3; page 9 alone does not confirm that these are the two panels already joined.

The moving large panel is mapped to node 21 ('side panel 35x25 (1)'), the opposite side panel, because it is a large panel that ends in contact with node 1 (large-component contact candidate [1,21], gap 0.0 m) and would complete an open three-sided frame. The drawing does not distinguish node 21 from node 2 (bottom panel, which contacts node 3) or node 4 (back panel, which contacts both 1 and 3), so this mapping is an inference.

Node 1 ('top panel 35x25') is drawn as an upright panel in the existing corner on page 9, while its source transform is horizontal in the finished cabinet. Its correspondence is inferred from the prior step and from its contact with node 21, not from matching illustrated orientation.

Node 3 ('side panel 35x25') is mapped to the other stationary panel of the corner. Because nodes 3 and 21 are symmetric opposite side panels, the assignment of which one is fixed and which one moves is inferred from the prior plan, not proven by the drawing.

The 0.10 m upward start offset is an inferred presentation gap; the manual gives no travel distance. The downward direction is inferred from the arrow as a vertical drop in parent coordinates, but the real assembly may require a different approach path or a tilted insertion.
A pure vertical drop may sweep the moving panel edge through the mating edge region before reaching its final position; collision and connector insertion are not modeled.
No torque, turn count, cam-lock rotation, or fastener tightening sequence is proposed because none of these is readable for this step.
The illustration could instead depict adding the second side panel to a back-and-side subassembly rather than to a top-and-side subassembly; if so, this node mapping and motion are not valid.
